summary: Round 6, test-reviewer. Scope is the one prose line changed since round 5; the code-only staged diff still hashes to 28ac1467c7f9, byte-identical to the tree both roles passed at round 3, so the tests are not re-reviewed. Every checkable claim in the new baselines/review.txt:36 line was verified against .harness/review and the staged tree: rounds 2 (cf0286e7) and 3 (28ac1467) are pass from both roles with minors only; round 1 (e60bf990) is changes-requested carrying blocking M4.47-R1a (the discarded Seal, described accurately including 'ADR-0037 rejected alternative (c) arriving through a race') plus minor M4.47-R1c, the stale javadoc, which this file's vocabulary two entries above (M4.10c, 'PROSE ONLY') does classify as prose; round 4's finding did quote 'EVERY ROUND FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN CODE, none in prose' and round 5's did quote 'ONLY ROUND 1 WAS CHANGES-REQUESTED' with round 4's own verdict as the counterexample; 'two of round 2's minors were that the production fix was UNPINNED' matches the atOrigin-to-constant survivor and the missing rule-20 faulted-sweep assertion; 'one overturned my reading of recoverChainEnd()' matches M4.47-R2a, which measured a lease release rather than a request saving; and 'seven tests' is exactly the count of @Test methods added by the staged diff (2 ChainReplayEmptyOriginTest, 3 LocalSequencerSealRaceTest, 1 LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest, 1 CommitProtocolSimulationTest). On stability: I could not construct a round that falsifies this draft the way rounds 4 and 5 falsified their predecessors. The self-falsifying shape needs a universal or exclusive quantifier over the verdicts on this line ('EVERY ROUND', 'ONLY ROUND 1'); this draft has none. 'Two drafts of this sentence were each falsified' names two specific past drafts and two specific catching rounds, both permanently true, and carries no 'only', so a third falsification would leave it an undercount rather than a falsehood -- which is why declining the count is the right call and not evasion. The one remaining universal, 'every round after it is about THIS LINE', is true now (rounds 4, 5 and 6 all carry findings on baselines/review.txt:36 and nothing else) and is falsified only by a round that moves code, at which point the entry is rewritten wholesale anyway; it is not falsifiable by the act of recording a verdict on the line. On evasion: no. The categories are all there, including that round 1 was blocking and that rounds 4 and 5 each found this line false, and the omission runs AGAINST the author -- the enumeration stops at round 5, so the entry under-claims the justification for exceeding the cap rather than over-claiming it. The pointer to .harness/review is legitimate rather than a dodge to an unreadable place: review.md itself cites .harness/review as the record, and scripts/review_rounds.py -- which this same line names as the owner of the count -- reads that directory, so deferring to it is the project's own mechanism, not a deflection. It is machine-local (.gitignore:12) and untracked, so the count is not recoverable from a clone; that is a property of the whole mechanism, not of this line, and every checkable fact this line does state is stated inline. Prior open findings, dispositions: M4.47-R1a fixed at round 2 and pinned by three tests in LocalSequencerSealRaceTest, including the open-only interleave that discriminates landed.sequence() > 0 from > 1 and the racing-chain-longer-than-sealRedriveBudget case that R2a asked for; M4.47-R4a and M4.47-R5a are both addressed by this draft. One minor below, which does not block and probably should not be fixed.

findings.title: 'Round 5 reviews its correction' is present tense, and this file's convention makes present tense mean the round now underway -- which is round 6
findings.finding: Every other round in the line is past tense ('Round 4 reviewed this line and found the sentence above false'); the switch to present for round 5 is the same device M4.10d uses ('Round 6 reviews that correction and a note moved to M4.10f, no production change') and M4.10c uses ('ROUND 6 IS PROSE ONLY'), where it identifies the round the entry is being reviewed in. Here that round is 6, not 5. review_rounds.py resolves the staged tree to 6; the prose stops at 5. This is the residue of round 4's own part (c) -- 'the entry never says what round 4 is, so a reader gets review_rounds.py counting four rounds against prose accounting for three' -- recurring one round later, in the direction that understates the author's case. It is a minor and not a major because the sentence is not false as a statement about what round 5 did, and because the line explicitly declines exhaustive enumeration and names the authoritative source, so the residue is one round of shape rather than a wrong fact. ⚠️ ACTING ON THIS IS PROBABLY WRONG, per review.md's minors-land and this line's own history: rewriting it as 'round 6 reviews this draft' rebuilds exactly the present-tense pointer that round 7 would falsify, which is the defect two drafts running. The only stable form is the tense, not the enumeration: 'Round 5 reviewed its correction' is invariant under any number of further rounds and is a one-word change, and leaving the sentence exactly as it stands is also defensible.
findings.failure_scenario: An auditor doing what this line invites -- running scripts/review_rounds.py against the landed tree, or listing the M4.47 verdicts in .harness/review -- gets six rounds against an entry whose narrative ends at five, with the last one written as though it were still in progress. baselines/review.txt is append-only, so the entry ships permanently describing a round that was not the last one, in the file whose only purpose is honesty about round counts. The reader's most likely inference is the wrong one in the author's favour by omission and against it in fact: either that round 5 was the final round and the entry was written before its verdict landed, or that a sixth round happened and was left out. Both readings cost the entry the credibility it spends three sentences building, and the second is the exact suspicion -- an author trimming the record -- that round 5's own failure_scenario names.
